chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: Catlett's dynamics and why the right drummer makes or breaks a big band
summary: Sid Catlett could explode or whisper; Saunders heard Basie sound bad in Rotterdam with the wrong drummer before Butch Miles joined.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: So it came right down to beat, time.
Gus Johnson or Jo, when he was hot.
When he was hot, right, right.

Oh, yeah, he was -- well, see, we talked about that touch and that feel. Now, he had that shading type. And he could explode or he could play to a whisper. And this is what drumming really is all about. When you get in on that type of band. Because nothing stays at one level all the time. And then you have to have that type of a touch.

And this is why Basie is so hard. They have to really look around for -- when it comes to drummers, because, see, Freddy's not going anywhere. He's still there and he'll always be there, I guess, until he -- but they have to have that drummer that has that certain thing. And if he doesn't have it, he's not going to make it.

No, no, the whole band won't make it. I heard them in Rotterdam. And they had a drummer out of Detroit. I don't know what his name was. And, oh, I've never heard the band sound so bad. Same men -- Lockjaw, what's his name, with his wa-wa, and all --
Yeah, Al Grey and all of them. The same personnel, but that drummer changed the whole complexion. So they didn't keep him too long. Right after that they got Butch Miles.
Yeah, because in a big band, the drummer is really the heart.
Right, he's the heart. He can either make them or break them.
Who was it -- I think maybe it was if Jo Jones that said/the drummer doesn't feel good, the rest of the band is going to screw up.
Right, right, right, and that's true.
